title: The Kingdom Concept and Principle of Transformation
paragraphs: I want every young person to listen very carefully, because you are the key to what will happen in the world over the next 40 years. And if you learn what I am going to share with you today, you will be able to contribute to the world more effectively. I would like to begin with a brief summary of what we discussed with you in my previous session, namely the current situation in the world.

When I was recently in Brazil, where the Pope, the head of the Catholic Church, was also, we were both in the news in Brazil every day. And on his last day in Brazil, he held a press conference. During that press conference, the Pope was asked a question about same- sex marriage and homosexuality. And then, for the first time in my life, I heard a Pope speak in a way that bore witness to deep concern. What bothered me most, and I say it openly, is that the Pope gave his personal opinion.

You know that we, as men of God and representatives of Christ, when in official capacities, may not give a personal opinion on matters on which the Bible has already spoken. Do you understand that? If I am not in an official capacity and I am speaking with you, for example at a dining table, and you ask me for my opinion on something, then I may give you that opinion. But when I am in an official capacity, I have no right to give my opinion on something over which God has already passed judgment.

The duty of a leader in the body of Christ, who claims to represent the word of God, Jesus Christ, and his Father Jehovah, is that we must always uphold the integrity of the Scriptures, no matter how hard the waves crash against us or how the currents oppose us. And I am talking about current events, or the changing times in our social life. We must never make concessions to the Scripture texts that have already been spoken. And this is very serious to me. That is why I was very disappointed.

And I think we will feel the consequences of the Pope's statement for years to come. And I believe that we will largely not recover from this, because there are people who are waiting for credibility and confirmation of their worldview from people who are respected by others. And I am very concerned, for personally there is no one greater than Jesus Christ. No one is above the Bible and no man is smarter than God. So I am not going to submit to anyone's title at the expense of God's integrity.

Let me now explain what I think is going on, and that is this word: conformity. Write it down. The pressure to conform is what is at play today. The United Nations is one of the most dangerous organizations on Earth, because it has itself undergone a transformation for which it was not established.

Those of you old enough will remember that the United Nations was founded shortly after the Second World War, when millions of people had perished on the battlefield in their own countries and humanity, driven by national guilt, decided that they no longer wanted to fight. Let's talk our problems out. So they founded an organization, the United Nations, an evolution of an earlier group, the League of Nations. The United Nations was founded with the goal of preventing wars. That was it.

So if there was a conflict somewhere, they came together at the United Nations. The UN Council met, discussed the problems, and subsequently resolved them diplomatically so that there would be no more fighting. That was the goal. The United Nations, however, has evolved into something I would simply like to call the world government. The United Nations is now a government, but it is the government of the world, because it no longer only prevents wars. They want to prevent you from believing what you believe.

They want to interfere with your national social norms, your economic programs, your educational programs, your culture, and your spiritual values. They want to interfere in everything and they want to dictate who you are, how you are, what you believe and what you don't believe, what you accept and what you don't accept. And it doesn't matter what your government says.

The United Nations ignores your national belief systems, your economic norms, and they impose on you what they demand if you supposedly want to be accepted by the international community. This is very dangerous. So in fact, I have changed the name of the United Nations to the United Conformity of Nations. Conformity of Nations means that globalization requires all nations, societies, people, and communities to adapt to the world system.

So if you use a term like 'Christian nation', that means nothing to the United Nations. If you talk about your country's preamble, that means nothing to the United Nations. When you talk about your spiritual national heritage, that means nothing to the United Nations. Their position is: you can shape yourself or you starve. Starvation means they won't give you access to the World Bank. They will deny you access to international loans for your local programs.

They will prevent you from participating in the World Trade Organization. In other words, they could starve you as a nation if you do not conform. Conformity is dangerous. Write it down. Conformity requires you to give up your beliefs, values, principles, morality, and individuality. Conformity means that I no longer exist. You shape me. This therefore destroys the uniqueness of a people. In other words, there is a principle in the Bible called a world government. It is stated in the Bible as a principle.

I'm not really into prophesying and all those prophetic things, but believe me, I'm starting to think that this is very possible and close at hand, because the UN is really preparing to become the world government, and in a way that I believe will be the cause of war, rather than its prevention. Because some countries, particularly Islamic and Hindu countries, will oppose the United Nations.

Instead of bringing peace, people will resist the pressure to conform and literally take up arms to attack the UN peacekeeping force and burn down the headquarters. And people do not understand that not everyone is willing to adapt. Now, I don't know how it is with the small states in the Caribbean, but when you are a small state, you sometimes think that your size is all you have. But let me tell you something: you don't have to be big to be great.

A country with 350,000 inhabitants defeated a country with 350 million inhabitants at the Olympic Games. That means that if God could do it in sports, and you are not hearing me, He can also do it economically, socially, and especially spiritually. Conformity therefore means destroying your uniqueness. And please write this down. The entire world is therefore going through a period of change. Change is always an attack on your beliefs. Let me quickly give you a list of things to write down.

We see changes in what I call our traditional values. We also see changes in our moral standards, or in the systems we have considered workable. Change also influences our cultural norms. Everyone talks about cultural norms. That word 'standards' is important. In fact, the word ' norms' is the Hebrew root of the word for law. The Hebrew word for law is 'normos'. N O M O S. It actually means 'that which is normal'. That is the law.

So when God created the Ten Commandments, for example, he created what the cultural norms should be. In other words, it is culturally normal not to commit adultery. Hm. It is culturally normal not to steal. Yes. It is culturally normal not to lie. These are the Ten Commandments. It is culturally normal to take a day off and rest. Culturally normal. You might still remember that a previous government decided to make Sunday a shopping day. Some of you might be wondering why there was so much objection to that.

Because it was customary in our culture to take a day off. But the government at the time changed that entire norm. They broke the law that we considered normal. And now people are dying of stress all over the Bahamas because they are not resting. And Shabbat stands for rest. It is a cultural norm not to work yourself to death to earn money. Take a day off. Amen. Some of you pay for a house and never enjoy it. You pay for a car and are n't going to drive around in it. Why? Too busy working for that car.

Take a day off for what you have achieved. These are cultural norms. We also see changes that affect our traditional belief system, our traditional rules, and our traditional laws. And that is where change affects us. And this is what I consider to be the pursuit of change. The goal of the contemporary movement for global social change is to move away from time-tested principles and values ​​established by our Creator. That is the change. They are trying to make us deviate from what? Proven principles and values.

It is now being investigated whether these principles and values ​​are beneficial for societal development. But because we want to change things, we want to change everything. This is very dangerous. Secondly, the urge for change in our postmodern world is even willing to violate the law of nature, which I cannot believe. In other words, they are trying to tell nature: change. The problem with nature is that it doesn't listen to you. For example, they want to pass laws to turn your rectum into an entrance.

The problem is that your rectum is a natural organ that God placed in your body for the elimination of waste. So no law in a courtroom, a law in a senate, a law in a court, or a law in a parliament can turn your rectum into an entrance. That's right. You can use it however you want, but you cannot change the law of nature. They are trying to change the natural law of reproduction. Yes. A man and a woman have children. You cannot pass a law and say: " No, I am going to have two male children."

Because the law of nature ignores your law, and the two of you cannot have children. So you have to borrow or adopt other people's children. Thirdly, change is inevitable. We need to understand that. But we must never change at the expense of principles. Principles are eternal. Let me briefly explain what I mean. You were created by God to continue creating without breaking his laws. God gave you the power to rule over the earth, but not against his laws.

Secondly, the creator expected growth and progress within the context of the divinely inherent laws of nature. God wants you to grow. He wants you to make progress within the context of the law. Thirdly, true change is growth and development within the boundaries of inherent natural and spiritual laws. That is true development. For example, you might want to drill for oil in the waters around the Bahamas. That is a development decision. But you also have to consider that that oil can leak and destroy the reefs.

If the reefs die, they will destroy our fish stocks. The dead fish will deplete our protein source, which means our children will become malnourished. You will have to import food from other countries that make money off you, purely to feed your children. You are then completely dependent on them if they are willing to feed you due to a development decision regarding oil. Therefore, there are certain laws of nature that God has established. And this brings us to point four. Write it down.

Natural laws and spiritual laws are protected by conscience and creation. You know when you are doing something wrong. You cannot tell me that your conscience does not speak to you when you break a law of nature. The problem is that you ignore your conscience. Yes. Whatever you do in secret that is inherently wrong, you know it is wrong, but you do it anyway, whether for pleasure or under pressure. Your conscience is the voice of God. Yes.

And when we pollute a river, when we throw waste into the ocean from our boats, we know deep in our hearts that something is wrong. Right? If we throw a cup out the window, a little alarm bell goes off in your head: "You should have saved that cup until you were home." But you ignore your conscience and throw the cup away. But your conscience was built in by God to keep your convictions in check. That brings me to the next point. Change. Write this down. To move forward, grow, and develop, change is necessary.

I am not against change. But this is the point you must remember: all true change must take place within the boundaries of natural and spiritual principles and laws. There must be a law that protects you against a total change that makes you disappear completely out of nowhere. You will break that law, purely for your pleasure. Listen, smoking weed is pleasant. Using cocaine. Woo! The high is indescribable. Injecting heroin into your veins makes you feel like you are in heaven. These are all forms of pleasure.

But the price of that pleasure... You break the laws of your body and your body gives out. You become a plant that staggers down the street day or night and sells your body for the next shot, or sells your mother's phone and television for the next shot. You break everything purely for your pleasure, because you think there is no law. But there is a law that restricts every action. Therefore, it is important that we do not break the laws that God has instituted.

Let me put it this way: not all change is improvement, progress, or progressive development. Not all change. So we have to decide what we should and shouldn't change. And this is what I want you to remember: everything will change. But the paradox is that change is only possible where something remains constant. That means we must be careful about what we change. Not everything needs to be changed. And some things are created to remain unchanged. Do you agree with that? Of course.

Suppose I decide to change your nose and turn it upside down, and then it starts to rain. What happens to you then? You are drowning. See? So never change your nose. I don't care how many cosmetic procedures you have done. Don't turn your nose upside down. Why not? There is a law of nature. It is falling. Okay? So, there are a few things you need to be careful with. Some things are made to stay the same and never change. And number six: never confuse change with growth. Write that down. Never confuse anything?

Change with growth. Some people say: "Well, to grow as a country, we have to change everything." That is a lie. Never believe that change is not necessarily growth. For example, you initially weighed 120 kilos, then 180, 200. Now you have gained weight, but that is not to your advantage. The doctor says: "We have a problem with your heart, a problem with your blood pressure. We have a problem with all your arteries." Now you run the risk of diabetes. So not all change is growth.

Another example: do you know what a tumor is? A tumor is a healthy cell that has grown too fast. That is what a tumor is. A tumor is not a bad cell. It is a good cell. But something went wrong in the chromosome combination that codes for multiplication, causing that cell to grow too fast and become a parasite to the body. It sucks blood from the blood vessels and becomes cancer. So there is growth, but no development. What exactly do we mean by this? Please write this down. 10 things you should never change.

Let me give them to you. Number one, 10 things. Number one: never change principles. Number two: never change the goals of things. For example: the purpose of a knife is to cut things like meat and vegetables. Do not change it to slit people's throats. A car is made to take you from point A to point B according to traffic rules. The problem is that you have the power, the will, to drive your car from the jetty into the water. No one can stop you. Your personal will. This is your car. You have your rights. You are free.
